strings.name: Barack Obama
strings.summary: Obama was the first African American president of the United States, serving from 2009 to 2017. He advanced from community organizing and state politics to national office, pursuing economic stimulus, health insurance reform and multilateral diplomacy. Counterterrorism operations, civilian casualties from drone strikes and executive power drew criticism. After leaving office, he continued civic and youth leadership work.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: As the first African American US president, he advanced health insurance reform and participated in responses to the financial crisis and international climate negotiations.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: BA, Columbia University (1983); JD, Harvard University (1991)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Health insurance reform
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Signed the Affordable Care Act, expanding coverage and protections for people with pre-existing conditions.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Economic response and diplomacy
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Pursued post-crisis recovery measures, the Iran nuclear agreement and normalization with Cuba.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Presidential Center opened
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Spoke at the opening ceremony of the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Completed two presidential terms
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Continued civic work through his foundation, writing and public appearances.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Addressed drone-strike criticism
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Acknowledged civilian deaths that should not have occurred and responded to accountability concerns.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Advanced diplomatic agreements
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The United States joined the Iran nuclear agreement and restored diplomatic relations with Cuba.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Signed health reform
strings.timeline.event-05.text: The Affordable Care Act became a central institutional achievement of his domestic agenda.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Inaugurated as president
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Became the 44th president and subsequently signed economic stimulus legislation responding to the Great Recession.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Elected to the US Senate
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Won the Illinois Senate seat, moving into national politics.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Elected state senator
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Won election to the Illinois Senate for a term starting the following year.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Graduated from Harvard Law School
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Had become the first African American president of the Harvard Law Review; subsequently worked in civil rights law.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Hawaii
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Honolulu and spent part of his childhood in Indonesia.
